entry.title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts 2,895 interactions among human mitochondrial proteins
entry.summary: Texas A&M AgriLife Research screened 630,003 protein pairs from about 1,100 human mitochondrial proteins with AlphaFold-Multimer and identified 2,895 likely interactions, more than half not previously reported, giving 85 uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners. The paper appeared in… (Discovery - Texas A&M AgriLife Research and Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis; announced 2026-11-05)

entry.title: Claude-assisted discovery of an Apache ActiveMQ Classic code-injection flaw
entry.summary: Horizon3.ai reports a remote code execution flaw in ActiveMQ Classic, introduced about 13 years earlier, that chains the Jolokia management API with network-connector VM transports. Apache rates it important and fixes it in 5.19.4 and 6.2.3. (Vulnerability - Horizon3.ai and Apache ActiveMQ; announced 2026-04-07)

entry.title: Claude finds a FreeBSD RPCSEC_GSS kernel stack overflow
entry.summary: FreeBSD advisory SA-26:08 describes a stack overflow in the RPCSEC_GSS code that can allow remote code execution in the kernel, with no workaround, affecting all supported versions. It credits Nicholas Carlini using Claude, Anthropic. (Vulnerability - Anthropic and FreeBSD Project; announced 2026-03-26)

entry.title: Hacktron's AI agent finds a BeyondTrust remote-support command injection
entry.summary: Hacktron reports an OS command injection in BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access, rated critical with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.9 and a variant of CVE-2024-12356 on the same WebSocket endpoint. BeyondTrust published advisory BT26-02 on 6 February 2026. (Vulnerability - Hacktron AI and BeyondTrust; announced 2026-02-06)

entry.title: o3 helps find a Linux kernel ksmbd use-after-free
entry.summary: Independent researcher Sean Heelan reports a use-after-free of sess->user in the ksmbd session-logoff handler, reachable when a second connection binds to the same session. The fix removes the free in smb2pdu.c and is tagged for stable backporting. (Vulnerability - Sean Heelan; announced 2025-05-22)

entry.title: Unrealistic emissions scenarios help AI climate models prepare for unfamiliar futures
entry.summary: MIT researchers with Imperial College London designed a small synthetic set of deliberately unrealistic emissions scenarios to train climate emulators, which normally need six to eight full Earth system model runs that each take months. The method needs only one model run, and the emulator… (Discovery - MIT; Imperial College London; announced 2026-11-12)

entry.title: Writing seen in PHerc. 306B for the first time in 2000 years
entry.summary: Vesuvius Challenge awarded a $50K First Letters Prize for scroll PHerc. 306B, where the winning submission reached the 10-character target and the papyrology team agreed on a reading, tentatively a Greek phrase with parallels in Aristotle and Philodemus. Ink was detected by multiplying two models… (Discovery - Vesuvius Challenge; announced 2026-11-02)

entry.title: Evo 2 uses in-context learning to design de novo regulatory sequences with only tens of examples
entry.summary: Arc Institute reports that Evo 2 designs functional regulatory sequences from 4 to 64 in-context examples without extra training, with 30-50% yield. Of nine AI-designed enhancers delivered by AAV to mice, seven drove detectable expression and two labeled layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons with 73%… (Discovery - Arc Institute; Stanford University; announced 2026-10-29)

entry.title: ElectrolyteGPT can generate new formulations for battery development
entry.summary: University of Chicago researchers trained a GPT model with a new notation (fLine) to generate complete battery electrolyte formulations, including solvent ratios, salt concentrations and temperature. Several AI-proposed compositions were synthesized and, per the release, performed on par with the… (Discovery - University of Chicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering; announced 2026-06-03)

entry.title: Claude-assisted discovery of a Firefox WebAssembly JIT flaw
entry.summary: Mozilla disclosed a WebAssembly JIT miscompilation vulnerability and credited researchers using Claude. Its advisory rates the impact high and lists Firefox 148 as the fixed release. This record covers one CVE, not the total findings in the Mozilla collaboration. (Vulnerability - Mozilla and Anthropic; announced 2026-02-24)

entry.title: Big Sleep identifies an undisclosed SQLite vulnerability
entry.summary: Google reports that Big Sleep, guided by threat intelligence, identified CVE-2025-6965 while the flaw was known to threat actors and at risk of exploitation. Google says its intervention prevented the anticipated use; this is not evidence of an observed successful hack. (Vulnerability - Google Project Zero, Google DeepMind and Google Threat Intelligence; announced 2025-07-15)

entry.title: Big Sleep finds a SQLite memory-safety bug before release
entry.summary: The team reports an AI-agent finding in development code that maintainers corrected on the reporting day. Project Zero states that the defect never reached an official SQLite release, so released users were not affected. (Vulnerability - Google Project Zero and Google DeepMind; announced 2024-11-01)

entry.title: AI-generated fuzzing reveals an OpenSSL memory-access flaw
entry.summary: An AI-generated fuzz target revealed an issue in low-level elliptic-curve handling. OpenSSL rates it low severity because vulnerable application use is considered unlikely and the problematic inputs do not arise in ordinary X.509 certificate processing. (Vulnerability - Google Open Source Security Team and OpenSSL; announced 2024-10-16)

entry.title: GPT-5 helps solve a 40-year-old problem about Nesterov's accelerated gradient
entry.summary: Ernest Ryu (UCLA) proved why Nesterov's accelerated gradient method, introduced in 1983, remains stable despite the extra momentum that makes it faster. GPT-5's turning point was a rewrite of the equations: not correct as given, but with a structure Ryu then developed and proved himself, over… (Discovery - OpenAI and University of California, Los Angeles; announced 2025-11-24)

entry.title: CorrDiff: kilometer-scale weather forecasts with generative AI
entry.summary: A diffusion model takes atmospheric data from 25-kilometer to 2-kilometer scale and also predicts variables absent from the inputs, such as radar reflectivity. The paper appeared the same day in Communications Earth and Environment; the initial model was tuned on Taiwan data with the Central… (Discovery - NVIDIA; announced 2025-02-24)

entry.title: LinearDesign: more stable mRNA sequences designed by an algorithm
entry.summary: The algorithm, based on a parsing technique from natural-language processing, finds the most stable mRNA sequence for a given protein in about eleven minutes. According to Baidu’s press release, whose study appeared in Nature, sequences produced this way showed greater stability, protein… (Discovery - Baidu Research; announced 2023-05-02)

entry.title: Signs of hypertension detected by a smartwatch
entry.summary: Prospective study of 196 people at five US sites, compared with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure measurement: 65.8% sensitivity and 90.0% specificity for screening, and 78.4% and 90.9% in the confirmatory test (48 participants). A feasibility study; it does not replace the cuff, and many cases… (Discovery - Google Research; announced 2026-11-05)

entry.title: First 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle, with Claude
entry.summary: Claude searched protein databases, designed DNA constructs, reduced purification from about three days to about 90 minutes, and processed cryo-EM data into an initial model in 34 hours. The result is a particle made of 96 copies of a bacteriophage protein, with about 25% more internal volume than… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-11-04)

entry.title: Agentic cheminformatics: new macrocycles from literature analysis
entry.summary: An agent using Cheminformatics Skills for Antigravity collected thousands of compounds analogous to crizotinib and lorlatinib, analyzed 568, and proposed new rigidified macrocycles with synthesis routes in about an hour. The proposals are computational hypotheses that still need to be synthesized… (Discovery - Google DeepMind; announced 2026-11-03)

entry.title: Claude's early progress in drug development
entry.summary: Anthropic reports early results with six partners: a CAR T-cell receptor design about 70% shorter that enabled immune cells to produce about 10 times more receptors; about 35,000 antibody designs in one month, yielding 20 candidates; and a document review that found all 11 human-identified issues… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-10-27)

entry.title: OpenAI presents three results in harmonic analysis, complexity, and quantum theory
entry.summary: OpenAI announces results on local smoothing, a disproof of the exponential time hypothesis, and the construction of quantum field theories. The source presents these as research results to be understood with academic groups: physical artifacts are not yet public, and independent verification is… (Discovery - OpenAI; announced 2026-10-26)

entry.title: Chest X-rays and AI for tuberculosis screening
entry.summary: Nexus AI says it has deployed Google Research's chest X-ray AI as a certified diagnostic tool at about 40 facilities in six countries: more than 25,000 X-rays assessed by over 90 clinicians, with response times under 45 seconds. These are author-reported deployment figures, with no sensitivity or… (Discovery - Google Research; announced 2026-10-23)

entry.title: ForTy 2020: global map of forest types at 10 meters
entry.summary: A 10-meter map classifies each land area into six forest or land-use types (including primary forest, plantations, and tree crops), with an initial time series from 2017–2025. Validation across more than 9,000 sites identifies the correct type in 90% of cases and distinguishes forest from… (Discovery - Google DeepMind, Google Research, World Resources Institute, IIASA; announced 2026-10-22)

entry.title: GPT-Rosalind agents connect genetic perturbations and neuronal signals
entry.summary: Analysis of a CRISPR atlas of mouse brain cells identified differences between Tsc1 and Tsc2 and a possible relationship between DCTN1 and cholesterol regulation. Experts assessed the interpretations, but the proposed mechanisms remain hypotheses to be tested in new experiments. (Discovery - OpenAI, PerturbAI and Scripps Research; announced 2026-10-21)

entry.title: AI-assisted ultrasound for dating pregnancy
entry.summary: Prospective study of 385 pregnant women in Chicago and Nairobi: the model estimates gestational age from scans taken by minimally trained operators with a mean error of 4.18 days, non-inferior to the 4.48 days of expert sonographers. This is a non-inferiority result from only two sites, both… (Discovery - Google Research; announced 2026-10-21)

entry.title: Claude designs binders against five scorpion neurotoxins
entry.summary: In a mostly autonomous 64-hour campaign, Claude designed minibinders against five neurotoxins. External labs tested 211 designs, 17 of which met the criteria; the best (Cn2-B1 and Cn2-B2) had affinities in the low nanomolar range. Only recombinant toxins were tested, with no neutralization tests… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-10-20)

entry.title: Claude designs more efficient quantum circuits
entry.summary: Claude designed circuits for eight basic operations (chemistry, optimization, physical simulation, and number theory), assessed by an automated verifier. In several cases they outperform the best published circuits; for example, a point addition used 17 times fewer gates at the cost of 12% more… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-10-16)

entry.title: AI agents in the lab: aptamers and proteins designed in a closed loop
entry.summary: AI agents designed DNA aptamers and protein binders, which were then tested in the lab over multiple rounds. Target success rates reached 33.5% for myoglobin and 42.1% for α-thrombin (98.5% specificity). The post summarizes three arXiv papers whose peer review is unconfirmed; it also reports… (Discovery - Google Research; announced 2026-10-16)

entry.title: Searching for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
entry.summary: An agentic workflow searched UniProt for antimicrobial candidates in Streptococcus pseudopneumoniae and found a 97-amino-acid bacteriocin with no homologues among manually reviewed Swiss-Prot proteins. This is a computational candidate now undergoing laboratory validation; no potency or toxicity… (Discovery - Google DeepMind; announced 2026-10-15)

entry.title: Earth AI for public health: geospatial models across five use cases
entry.summary: The PDFM model increased the explained variance in MMR vaccination coverage from 16% to 22% across 146 counties on the US–Canada border, and improved weekly correct cholera-risk-area rankings in the DRC from 1.78 to 2.10. Gains for cardiovascular mortality and postpartum depression were small or… (Discovery - Google Research; announced 2026-10-06)

entry.title: SynthID Bio: watermarking for proteins and synthetic structures
entry.summary: Methods insert a detectable signal into protein sequences and predicted structures. For binders designed against three targets (VEGF-A, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, and PD-L1), watermarked designs matched the others in success rate and affinity. This is a proof of concept that needs to be made more robust… (Discovery - Google DeepMind; announced 2026-09-30)

entry.title: Catalysts without iridium or ruthenium for acidic oxygen evolution
entry.summary: An AI-guided, human-supervised platform assessed 2,942 catalysts and identified complex palladium oxides. InMnPdOx maintained an overpotential below 0.5 V for more than 1,000 hours in sulfuric acid at 10 mA/cm². This is a preprint and laboratory result, without validation in a PEM electrolyzer. (Discovery - Lila Sciences; announced 2026-09-24)

entry.title: Claude identifies a new enzyme system: array-associated reverse transcriptases
entry.summary: About 950 Claude agents searched a DNA-sequence database for 21 hours (210 million tokens) and flagged an uncharacterized enzyme system, found mostly in bacteriophages, with a DNA repeat array similar to CRISPR. Scientists performed the laboratory work; the function remains unknown, and the work… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-09-23)

entry.title: RetroChimera: predicting small-molecule synthesis
entry.summary: Published in Nature, the method combines a Transformer model (R-SMILES 2) and a template-based graph model (NeuralLoc) through a learned vote. In blind tests with expert chemists, 90% of complete routes were accepted, compared with 20–50% for the component models or a baseline, and nine of ten… (Discovery - Microsoft Research; announced 2026-09-21)

entry.title: Claude optimizes more than 30 open models for biology
entry.summary: In just under four weeks, Claude optimized over 30 models for structure, protein design, and genomics. They were on average four times faster with a small accuracy loss, and nearly twice as fast with identical outputs. It also created a low-memory mode for systems over 10,000 tokens on a single… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-09-17)

entry.title: OpenAI proposes a solution to the Navier–Stokes problem
entry.summary: OpenAI announces a proof that three-dimensional solutions to the Navier–Stokes equations can develop a singularity in finite time and publishes a text formalized in Lean. This is the source's claim: this record does not establish community consensus, correctness of the artifacts, or recognition as… (Discovery - OpenAI; announced 2026-09-08)

entry.title: Codex agents perform measurements and calibrations on a six-qubit chip
entry.summary: Connected to MIT EQuS lab software, GPT-5.6 Sol selected parameters, ran measurements, and calibrated a six-qubit superconducting chip, measuring its frequencies and coherence. The demonstration covers known procedures on real hardware; weak or noisy signals sometimes required expert assistance… (Discovery - OpenAI and MIT EQuS; announced 2026-09-08)

entry.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: predictive map of human DNA variation
entry.summary: A precomputed database of predicted molecular effects for about 9 billion possible single-letter changes in the human genome, generated by AlphaGenome. Researchers can access it free through a portal and API. The predictions are a research tool, do not replace experiments, and are not validated… (Discovery - Google DeepMind; announced 2026-09-08)

entry.title: Claude formalizes Fermat's theorem in Lean
entry.summary: A proof of Fermat's Last Theorem fully machine-verified in Lean: Claude produced most of it independently over 11 days, with about 13 million lines and 29,500 intermediate theorems, and a comparator confirms that its statement matches Mathlib's. It follows a simplified version of Wiles's proof… (Discovery - Anthropic; announced 2026-09-04)

entry.title: WeatherNext 3: a global AI model for weather forecasting
entry.summary: A model that learns from real-time geostationary satellite data and produces hourly forecasts, at resolutions down to 5 km for temperature and humidity (about five times finer than WeatherNext 2). For short-term precipitation, Google reports improvements of up to 60% over NASA's IMERG. These are… (Discovery - Google DeepMind and Google Research; announced 2026-09-03)
